messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Memory
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Threat

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals → Memory
  - Memory → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Memory → Threat
  - Memory → Negative Appraisals
  - Threat → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Threat → Negative Appraisals

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Kofi had always taken pride in his work as a tailor, carefully crafting each garment with precision and attention to detail. But that was before the terrorist attack at the market where he used to buy fabric. The sounds of gunfire and screams still echoed in his mind, and the smell of smoke and blood lingered on his clothes. In the aftermath, Kofi found himself struggling to make sense of what had happened. He couldn't shake off the feeling that he was weak for not being able to protect himself or others (Weakness Belief). This self-doubt crept into every aspect of his life, making him question his ability to trust his own judgment (Self-Doubt). As a result, Kofi began to feel like he no longer belonged anywhere (Belong Nowhere), as if the attack had somehow severed his connection to the world around him. These negative appraisals took a toll on Kofi's daily life. He started spending long hours on his phone, scrolling through social media or playing games, in an attempt to distract himself from the memories of that day (Screen Escape). He would also pick arguments with his friends and family, creating drama as a way to shift his focus away from the trauma (Seeking Conflict). Making plans for the future seemed daunting, so Kofi simply avoided thinking about it altogether (Avoid Future Plans). But despite these attempts to escape, the memories of the attack lingered. Sometimes Kofi would recall the event in vivid detail, only to feel a strange sense of numbness, as if he was watching someone else's life unfold (Emotionless Recall). Other times, he would find himself stuck on specific moments, reliving them over and over like a film playing on repeat (Memory Replay). There were also gaps in his memory, moments that seemed lost forever, which only added to his frustration (Memory Gaps). These memories not only haunted Kofi but also made him hypervigilant. He would scan for exits whenever he entered a room or building (Scanning Exits), and feel safest when his back was against a wall, where he could see everything around him (Back to Wall). His constant state of alertness left him exhausted, yet he couldn't shake off the feeling that danger lurked around every corner (Hypervigilance). As Kofi's memories continued to plague him, they also reinforced his negative appraisals. He began to believe that he was indeed weak for not being able to overcome these memories (Weakness Belief). His self-doubt grew, and with it, the conviction that he no longer belonged anywhere (Belong Nowhere). The threat of danger seemed omnipresent, and Kofi's maladaptive strategies only intensified. He became more withdrawn, avoiding social interactions and spending most of his time alone in his small apartment above the tailor shop. His work suffered as a result, with orders piling up and customers beginning to lose patience. It was this downward spiral that finally brought Kofi to seek help. He realized that he couldn't keep living in a state of constant fear and self-doubt. With a sense of trepidation, he began to hope that therapy might offer him a way out of the darkness that had consumed his life since the attack.
